title: Coloring Rules: Add ability to display multiple coloring rules
description:
Packets matching multiple color filter rules now display all matching
colors simultaneously rather than only the first match.

Packet list rows show vertical candy-cane stripes for each matching
color filter. The display mode preference offers four options: Off,
Scrollbar Only, Full Stripes, and Shift Right (75% to 95%). In Full Stripes
mode the entire row is divided into equal-width stripes with optional style edges vertical/diagonal/bubble. In Shift Right mode the primary color fills xx% of
the row and additional colors appear as stripes in the remaining xx%.
The scrollbar minimap shows multi-color stripes for all non-Off modes.

A separate preference controls multi-color output in the packet details
pane and TShark field output (frame.coloring_rule.name /
frame.coloring_rule.string), allowing it to be enabled independently
of the packet list display.

Individual coloring rules can be temporarily paused via right-click on
any coloring rule name in the Frame tree. Paused rules are excluded
from stripe rendering and display with a [PAUSED] prefix in the tree.
Pause state persists per profile in a paused_filters file and survives
display filter changes and Wireshark restarts. A Resume All option
clears all paused rules at once.

color_filters_colorize_packet_all() collects all matching filters
during dissection and stores them in wmem_file_scope proto_data for
reuse by the row delegate, scrollbar painter, and packet details
dissector without re-running filter matching.

Conversation color filters are excluded from multi-color display.
Multi-color rendering respects packet priority (ignored/marked) and
the colorization toolbar toggle.

AI-Assisted: yes

notes.body:
## Overview

This feature extends that by showing all matching color rules simultaneously — as vertical candy-cane stripes in the packet list and scrollbar minimap, and as a full list of matching rule names in the packet details pane. The candy-cane stripes were added because on the initial development I had just used a vertical stripe. When this displayed I felt it caused the packets to run together visually. So I added the 45 degree angle to the inside of the paint to see if that would help the visualization. I believe that it does. Unfortunately I did not capture a screenshot of what 90 degree paint looked like.


## Preferences

All preferences are under **Edit → Preferences → Layout**.
![image](/uploads/39c4f17b780e5380fef2b3ce0e5bf69e/image.png){width=335 height=304}
 
### Packet list multi-color display mode (dropdown)

Controls whether and how multi-color stripes appear.

| Option | Packet list rows | Scrollbar minimap |
|---|---|---|
| **Off** (default) | single color | single color |
| **Scrollbar Only** | single color | stripes |
| **Full Stripes** | full-width stripes | stripes |
| **Shift Right (85%)** | 85%/15% stripes | stripes |

**Preference key:** `gui.packet_list_multi_color_mode`
**Values:** `off`, `scrollbar_only`, `full_stripes`, `shift_right`

### Display multiple colors in packet details (checkbox)

When enabled, the Frame tree in the packet details pane lists **all** matching color filter names and their filter strings — not just the first match. Also controls TShark multi-color output. Having this need is TShark is the reason I kept this as it’s own checkbox, and not just add it to the “display mode”

**Preference key:** `gui.packet_list_multi_color_details`
**Values:** `TRUE` / `FALSE` (default: `FALSE`)

 ![image](/uploads/02435bc9bcfc152c697d14146e2c958c/image.png){width=261 height=168}

## Display Modes

### Full Stripes

Each matching color filter gets an equal-width vertical stripe across the entire row. During initial development, stripes used straight vertical edges — but this caused adjacent packets to visually run together, making it hard to tell where one row ended and the next began. To solve this, the stripes were redesigned with diagonal 45° edges on each boundary, creating a **candy-cane pattern**. The diagonal offset (equal to the row height) gives each row a distinct visual rhythm that naturally separates packets from one another.

Text color is calculated from the average luminance of all background colors using ITU-R BT.709 perceptual coefficients:

luma = 0.2126 × red + 0.7152 × green + 0.0722 × blue
avg_luma = sum(all_lumas) / number_of_colors
text = black if avg_luma > 0.5, else white

I’m not a fan of this view, but it’s the first view I came up with when developing this feature.  When having light and dark coloring rules it becomes really difficult to see. So that’s what led me to the 85% view (as you’ll see next). I kept it here just in case someone might want it.
 ![image](/uploads/d47e65f7da4e26b9ece791950e88652b/image.png){width=484 height=113}

### Shift Right (85%)

Initial development used only full evenly-distributed stripes across the entire row — including the luminance-based text color calculation. However, when packets matched color filters with large variations in brightness (e.g., one very dark and one very light filter), the averaged text color sometimes produced poor readability across the row. The 85%/15% split was introduced to address this: the primary (first matching) color dominates at 85% of the row width, making the text color decision straightforward (use the primary filter's defined foreground color), while the remaining 15% shows equal-width stripes for all additional matching colors. Full Stripes mode is still available for users who prefer the evenly-distributed look.

The 85%/15% boundary uses a diagonal candy-cane edge matching the Full Stripes style. When only one color is active (all others paused), that single color fills 100% of the row.
 ![image](/uploads/480fff5d55ca7b6cbebeadefff999799/image.png){width=489 height=112}

### Scrollbar Only

No stripes in the packet list rows — the scrollbar minimap alone shows stripes. Useful for a clean list view while still seeing multi-color density at a glance in the minimap.

 ![image](/uploads/e9ff91f50e12d844cf58660836133a6b/image.png){width=487 height=109}


## Packet Details Pane

When **Display multiple colors in packet details** is enabled, the Frame tree shows all matching rules:


Frame 42: 74 bytes on wire
    Coloring Rule Name: Bad TCP
    Coloring Rule String: tcp.analysis.flags && !tcp.analysis.window_update
    Coloring Rule Name: HTTP
    Coloring Rule String: http || http2


Paused rules display with a `[PAUSED]` prefix:

    Coloring Rule Name: [PAUSED] Bad TCP
    Coloring Rule String: tcp.analysis.flags && !tcp.analysis.window_update

Conversation color filters (temporary filters prefixed with `___conversation_color_filter___`) are always hidden from this list.


## Pause / Resume Coloring Rules

Temporarily suppress individual color rules for the current session without permanently disabling them.

 ![image](/uploads/6478c62ca68705696bbcf02d1abdc0e0/image.png){width=480 height=433}


### How to Use

1. Open a packet's Frame tree in the details pane (requires **Display multiple colors in packet details** to be enabled)
2. Right-click any **Coloring Rule Name** entry
3. Select **Pause Coloring Rule** — that rule is removed from display immediately
4. The entry shows as **[PAUSED] RuleName** and is excluded from stripe rendering
5. Right-click the paused entry → **Resume Coloring Rule** to re-enable it
6. Right-click any entry → **Resume All Coloring Rules** to clear all paused rules at once

### Persistence

Paused rules are saved per profile to:
~/.config/wireshark/profiles/<profile_name>/paused_filters
One filter name per line. They survive display filter changes, file loads, and Wireshark restarts. Each profile maintains its own independent pause state.

## TShark Usage

The `frame.coloring_rule.name` and `frame.coloring_rule.string` fields expose multi-color data in TShark. The `gui.packet_list_multi_color_details` preference must be `TRUE` for multiple matches to be reported per packet.

### Show all matching color rule names per packet

tshark -r capture.pcapng \
  -o gui.packet_list_multi_color_details:TRUE \
  --color \
  -T fields \
  -e frame.number \
  -e frame.coloring_rule.name \
  -c 20

### Show matching rule names and filter strings

tshark -r capture.pcapng \
  -o gui.packet_list_multi_color_details:TRUE \
  --color \
  -T fields \
  -e frame.number \
  -e frame.coloring_rule.name \
  -e frame.coloring_rule.string \
  -c 20

Sample output when multiple rules match:

1   Bad TCP,HTTP   tcp.analysis.flags && !tcp.analysis.window_update,http || http2
2   HTTP           http || http2
3   Bad TCP,HTTP   tcp.analysis.flags && !tcp.analysis.window_update,http || http2

### Override details preference on the command line

# Disable multi-color details output regardless of saved preference
tshark -r capture.pcapng \
  -o gui.packet_list_multi_color_details:FALSE \
  --color \
  -T fields -e frame.number -e frame.coloring_rule.name


## Implementation Details

### Core Color Filter System — `epan/color_filters.c/h`

- `color_filters_colorize_packet_all()` — returns all matching color filters, not just the first
- `color_filter_set_session_disabled()` / `color_filter_is_session_disabled()` — pause/resume individual filters by name
- `color_filter_resume_all()` — clear all paused filters at once
- `color_filter_write_paused()` / `color_filter_read_paused()` — persist pause state to/from profile file

### Preferences — `epan/prefs.h`, `epan/prefs.c`

- `gui_packet_list_multi_color_mode` (enum) — Off / Scrollbar Only / Full Stripes / Shift Right 85%
- `gui_packet_list_multi_color_details` (bool) — show all matches in packet details and TShark output

### Packet List Record — `ui/qt/models/packet_list_record.cpp/h`

- Added `color_filters_` (GSList\*) and `color_filter_count_` members
- Added `matchingColorFilters()`, `hasMultipleColors()`, `colorFilterCount()` accessors
- Calls `color_filters_colorize_packet_all()` when any multi-color feature is active
- Stores the full match list in `wmem_file_scope()` proto_data so packet-frame.c can access it without re-running filter matching

### Multi-Color Delegate — `ui/qt/models/multi_color_packet_delegate.cpp/h`

New `QStyledItemDelegate` that handles custom row rendering:

- Skips rendering for Off and Scrollbar Only modes, or when the packet has only one match
- Respects ignored > marked > colored priority hierarchy
- Respects the "Draw packets using coloring rules" toolbar toggle (`recent.packet_list_colorize`)
- Skips custom rendering when a row is selected or hovered (preserves Qt selection/hover feedback)
- Draws full-width trapezoid stripes with diagonal candy-cane edges (Full Stripes mode)
- Draws 85%/15% split with diagonal boundary edge (Shift Right mode)
- Calculates text color from average luminance (Full Stripes) or uses primary filter's foreground color (Shift Right)

### Packet List — `ui/qt/packet_list.cpp`

- `setColumnDelegate()` installs the multi-color delegate for Full Stripes and Shift Right modes only
- `drawNearOverlay()` (scrollbar minimap) draws stripes for all non-Off modes, skipping session-disabled filters

### Packet Details — `epan/dissectors/packet-frame.c`, `epan/dissectors/file-file.c`

- Retrieves stored match list from proto_data using `proto_frame` key
- When `gui_packet_list_multi_color_details` is enabled, adds all matching filter names and strings to the Frame tree
- Paused filters display with `[PAUSED]` prefix so users can still right-click to resume them even when all rules are paused

### GUI Preferences — `ui/qt/layout_preferences_frame.cpp/h/ui`

- Dropdown for mode: Off / Scrollbar Only / Full Stripes / Shift Right (85%)
- Checkbox for packet details multi-color display

### ProtoTree — `ui/qt/proto_tree.cpp`

- Context menu on `frame.coloring_rule.name` fields offers: Pause Coloring Rule / Resume Coloring Rule / Resume All Coloring Rules
- Only shown when `gui_packet_list_multi_color_details` is enabled
- Uses `QTimer::singleShot(0)` to defer redissection until after the context menu closes, preventing crashes when dissecting while a packet is actively displayed
- Emits `redissectPacketsRequested()` signal to trigger full redissection so the Frame tree updates immediately

### Main Window — `ui/qt/wireshark_main_window.cpp`

- Connects `ProtoTree::redissectPacketsRequested` to `WiresharkMainWindow::redissectPackets`
- Automatically clears paused filters when a new capture file is opened

---

## Data Flow

1. **Colorize:** `PacketListRecord::dissect()` calls `color_filters_colorize_packet_all()` → stores full match list in `wmem_file_scope()` proto_data keyed by `proto_frame`
2. **Rows:** `MultiColorPacketDelegate::paint()` reads match list → draws candy-cane stripes
3. **Scrollbar:** `drawNearOverlay()` reads match list → draws minimap stripes
4. **Details:** `packet-frame.c` reads proto_data → adds all names/strings to Frame tree
5. **Pause:** `color_filter_set_session_disabled()` → redissect → stripe and Frame tree update to reflect pause state



## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `epan/color_filters.h/c` | `colorize_packet_all()`, pause/resume API, profile persistence |
| `epan/prefs.h/c` | New preferences and enum |
| `epan/dissectors/packet-frame.c` | Multi-color details display, PAUSED prefix |
| `epan/dissectors/file-file.c` | Multi-color details display |
| `ui/qt/models/packet_list_record.h/cpp` | Store and expose full match list |
| `ui/qt/models/multi_color_packet_delegate.h/cpp` | **New:** candy-cane stripe rendering delegate |
| `ui/qt/packet_list.h/cpp` | Delegate setup, scrollbar painting |
| `ui/qt/layout_preferences_frame.h/cpp/ui` | Preferences UI |
| `ui/qt/proto_tree.cpp` | Pause / Resume / Resume All context menu |
| `ui/qt/wireshark_main_window.cpp` | Redissect signal connection, clear paused on file open |
| `ui/qt/CMakeLists.txt` | Add new delegate to build |

@markspcs Something fishy about setting `has_color_info = true;` when `color_filter == NULL`.

Introduced by commit b77ce0d218 (Coloring Rules: Add ability to display multiple coloring rules). In the coloring-display block around packet-frame.c:1269–1341 (master branch as of 20.04.2026, not the line numbers here):

1. color_filter = pinfo->fd->color_filter can legitimately be NULL when every matching color rule is session-disabled ("all paused") — color_filters_colorize_packet_all() returns NULL as the primary but still populates the matches list.
2. Line 1279: if (matches && !has_color_info) has_color_info = true; flips has_color_info on even though color_filter is NULL.
3. Line 1295: if (has_color_info && fh_tree) enters the block.
4. If the user's gui_packet_list_multi_color_details pref is off, the conditional at line 1298 sends us into the else fallback at line 1323, which at line 1326 does strncmp(color_filter->filter_name, ...) — NULL deref → SIGSEGV.
I'll look at this a little bit more.

I've addressed this by dropping has_color_info entirely, as Jaap suggested. The two display paths now each guard themselves directly on color_filter.

While testing I also found a related stale proto_data issue that I addressed as well.

I hope this addresses all the concerns and problems, and again thank you for taking the time to find this issue.
